I'll read the council brief in full and follow it exactly.The brief is long; I’ll keep reading the rest so the vote is based on the full document.The brief names the files but not their contents. I’ll inspect the actual code, laws, and duplicates so the delete votes are grounded.I’ll inspect the guards, wrappers, canaries, and wallpaper laws next — those are the prime delete suspects.Next I’ll read the canaries, remaining guard code, and wrapper overlap so the votes name exact functions.I’ll check how the wrappers actually call the guards, and how much SKILL.md restates SPINE.DELETE LIST — ranked, in the format above

---

**[DELETE] `SPINE.md` PART VI · “The plan card and budget postures” — posture map, per-posture playbooks, and ENTRY/MINIMAL/NONE essays (`SPINE.md` lines 369–384 and 402–439) plus the routing-ledger epistemology essay (lines 468–478)**

EVIDENCE: Always-loaded. `PLAN-CARD.md` does not exist in this repo. `WAR CHEST` / `CRUISE` / `SHOESTRING` / `LIMP HOME` appear only inside `SPINE.md` (and a `legacy/` copy). Not in the 25-session usage table. The section describes knobs and a file the shop does not have; SPINE’s own words: “a method that describes knobs the harness lacks is a costume.” Previous councils relocated this kind of weight. It is still here, still billed on every summon, still unused.

Never-referenced-in-25-sessions is sufficient **when the named ritual was never run and the artifact it would produce does not exist.** That is this block. It is not sufficient for a rule followed under another alive name (see DEFEND).

COST IF WRONG: An orchestrator improvises spend instead of reading a posture table. The shop would notice as reckless fan-out or a frontier seat on grunt work — the same failure Gate-0, RIGHT-SIZE, and THE METER LAW already name. Those stay.

---

**[DELETE] `SKILL.md` · FUEL MODE (lines 59–72); THE LEGEND restatement (lines 48–54); PERSISTENT SEATS doctrine bullets (lines 89–101); THE RESERVE BENCH (lines 103–126); NON-NEGOTIABLES (lines 152–160)**

EVIDENCE: SKILL claims “this is a thin loader” then restates TRANSPORT LAW, METER LAW, THE NOTATION, and the invariant block. That restatement is how the Deck carried a stale v4.0 legend against SPINE’s v4.2 “for two days.” FUEL MODE is dated 2026-08-24, opt-in ADHD verbiage, not method. Always-loaded (~3.5k tokens) of copy that has already forked law once.

COST IF WRONG: A conductor narrates without a local color list, or forgets `always_approve` on a build ticket. THE NOTATION, THE TRANSPORT LAW, and the seats table (lines 78–87) still load. The shop would notice a missing 🟡➤ or a stalled headless build on the first dispatch.

---

**[DELETE] `SPINE.md` PART II · Doctrine 6 · THE LINEAGE ENGINE (lines 147–169)**

EVIDENCE: Usage 6 — loaded, never invoked. No `model-lineage-ledger.md` at project root. Weekly STANDINGS/RECALIBRATE never ran in 25 sessions. The shop bent the engine to describe a ledger nobody writes. “If session 26 will miss it, that case must be made” — it has not been.

COST IF WRONG: Routing memory stops accruing. They would notice when someone asks for “dispatch standings” and there is no ritual. `SPINE-WIRING.md` still records this box’s ledger path; `BENCH-LEDGER.md` still holds reserve track record.

---

**[DELETE] `mcp-seats/dispatch-guard.py` · `Lock`, `_lock_pid`, `_pid_alive`, `reserve`, `release`, `_expire`, `yield_report`, `find_events_csv`, `load_events`, and CLI subcommands `reserve` / `release` / `status` / `yield`**

**[DELETE] `mcp-seats/wmw_cursor_mcp.py` · `run_cursor` reservation block (lines 467–498) — the `guard.reserve` / lease path**

EVIDENCE: Added for today’s councils. Same authority as the adversary it claims to stop; store is plain JSON under `~`. Owner-token was added, then removed the same day because it broke the CLI. `yield` silently reported zero (wrong path, then wrong JSON shape) — a metric you must remember to run, duplicate of `bench-burn.py` + `read-meters.py`. An audit called the reservation path dead code that crashed; the fix was more code. `cwd` is not an OS boundary. This is ceremony with a security UI.

`preflight` is the one honest accident-prevention in this file. It stays (see DEFEND).

COST IF WRONG: N write-capable Cursor launches race the same headroom. The shop would notice as a spend spike on the vendor dashboard — the same dashboard `VENDOR-CHECKLIST.md` already says is the only control that binds cloud/IDE lanes. Wrapper coupling is loud: leftover `guard.reserve` would error, not fail open.

**[DELETE] `mcp-seats/allowance.py` (whole file)**

**[DELETE] `mcp-seats/wmw_cursor_mcp.py` · `_allowance`, `_allowance_window_s`, `_allowance_calls` (lines 191–232) and the CREDITS allowance gate (lines 430–439)**

**[DELETE] `SPINE.md` THE COUNCIL SEAT LAW · “Enforced, not merely written” paragraph (lines 785–791)**

EVIDENCE: Today. `status()` never counts calls; until today’s patch, “10/week” was enforced as 10 per 10 minutes. The store is a sticky note any yolo session can `grant --forever`. THE COUNCIL SEAT LAW is alive (86) as *ask-once, bound, expire*. The JSON file is the lie that those are machine-enforced. Deleting the file without deleting the wrapper hooks would fail-closed every credit model — so the hooks go with it.

COST IF WRONG: A metered seat spends without a file check. The conductor still has to ask (clauses 1–6 stay). They would notice a credit dispatch that nobody granted — the same way they notice any other unasked spend. The Cursor **council lock** (`COUNCIL_LOCK_*` in `wmw_cursor_mcp.py`) still trips a metered fan-out.

---

**[DELETE] `SPINE.md` PART V · THE AMENDMENT LAW (lines 334–336)**

EVIDENCE: Usage 6. Meta-rule: “choose the one that leaves a trace.” That rule is the accretion engine this council exists to stop. The scar already lives in `SPINE-PROVENANCE.md`. A law nobody cites, whose advice is “never delete,” is not earning its place on the always-loaded trunk.

COST IF WRONG: A later edit prefers a habit over an artifact. Provenance still tells the story; Part V mechanisms 5–6 (three lists, untestability is never evidence) stay.

---

**[DELETE] `SPINE.md` PART II · Doctrine 4 · THE SCALPEL IS A FEATURE (lines 136–140)**

EVIDENCE: Never invoked as a named doctrine. Anecdote. The operative lean default already lives in Gate-0 and RIGHT-SIZE DISPATCH (alive, 21). This council *is* the scalpel.

COST IF WRONG: The deaf-slot story vanishes from the engine. It is already a provenance-class war story, not a rule a conductor needs before the first dispatch.

---

**[DELETE] `SPINE.md` PART VI · The episode folder — SHOW credits, date-vs-name style law, and JPEG recipe (lines 526–548)**

EVIDENCE: No `episodes/` directory in this repo. The Deck “does NOT roll credits.” `~1280px` / quality ~70 / `.claude\uploads\` is wiring, not law. SHOW leakage into the always-loaded engine.

COST IF WRONG: A harvest folder isn’t created. Bottling would notice. Nothing in SKILL’s on-invocation checklist depends on this.

---

**[DELETE] `SPINE.md` PART VIII · Signature mechanic prose (lines 702–705) and the block-id footnote (lines 721–727)**

EVIDENCE: THE SIGNATURE MECHANIC usage 6. THE NOTATION is alive (93). “Every seat signs” is already in the invariant block (KEEP). The footnote about `v2026-07-22 r2` vs spine versions is how law becomes wallpaper: a comment about a comment.

COST IF WRONG: A seat forgets to sign. The invariant block and THE NOTATION still require it; the shop would notice unsigned lines the same way it does now.

---

**[DELETE] `SPINE.md` PART VI · “The three flips” (lines 642–650)**

EVIDENCE: Anecdote restating Principle 3. Never in the usage table. The load-bearing sentence (“seat map is mission state; lineage that produced the work does not approve it”) already lives in Part IV and the invariant block.

COST IF WRONG: A new conductor treats seat assignment as method-state. Principle 3 and review-dispatch still forbid self-review.

**[DELETE] `mcp-seats/armcheck.py` · check `"no lease left behind after a refused dispatch"` (lines 65–66)**

**[DELETE] `mcp-seats/armcheck.py` · source-string check `"cursor: spend ledger is NOT inside the playpen"` (lines 105–106)**

**[DELETE] `mcp-seats/armcheck.py` · default-mode “ALL ARMED” covering skipped 2b attack canaries (lines 127–130 and the `ALL ARMED` banner at line 201)**

EVIDENCE: The lease check cannot fail: the dispatch it runs is refused *before* `reserve`, and for a stretch today `reserve` crashed anyway. The ledger check reads source text, not behavior. Free mode skips every live write-attempt, then prints ALL ARMED. A canary that cannot fail, or that never attacks, is the green checkmark over dead code the brief named. The `--deep` behavioral canaries and the empty-repo preflight check are real; those stay.

COST IF WRONG: A broken reserve or a moved ledger string goes unnoticed by the free suite. `--deep` still attacks write-through-read-only. They would notice on a release run, which is when `--deep` is for.

**[DELETE] `FIELD-NOTES.md` (whole file)**

EVIDENCE: Appendix B of `SPINE-WIRING.md` is the same gotchas (agy exact-match `--model`, Codex “exploit” vocabulary, Gemini builds/images/reviews). Previous council relocated instead of deleting. Two files, one job, neither loaded on summon, both still to maintain.

COST IF WRONG: A habit of opening `FIELD-NOTES.md` finds nothing. Wiring Appendix B still has the croaks; SPINE already gates “load wiring before the first vendor call.”

---

**[DELETE] `MODEL-DISPATCH-GUIDE.md` (whole file)**

EVIDENCE: Opens with Jessie/James/Butch/Cassidy/the cat. This tier’s SKILL forbids character names. It is the playbook Doctrine 6 would recalibrate; Doctrine 6 never ran. Overlaps `SPINE-WIRING.md` arsenal + SKILL review-routing illustration.

COST IF WRONG: A conductor rediscovers “Codex for code review, Grok for skins.” Wiring and SKILL step 4 still say that.

**[DELETE] `legacy/` (whole tree: `legacy/cursor-native/{CURSOR-NATIVE.md,SKILL.md,SPINE.md}`, `legacy/SKILL-standalone.md`)**

EVIDENCE: Frozen copies of the engine. Already contradicting live SPINE (posture text duplicated; cursor-native still in the tree). Not loaded. Rot.

COST IF WRONG: Someone looking for the Cursor-native fork finds nothing. Git history still has it.

COST IF WRONG: A later trim cannot be re-applied from these files. That council’s SIGNED answers remain.

`docs/BAKEOFF-cursor-grok.md`, `docs/BAKEOFF-cursor-grok-ARMED.md`, `docs/BAKEOFF-house-grok.md`, `docs/BAKEOFF-house-grok.json`, `docs/H2H-cursor-grok.md`, `docs/H2H-cursor-grok-ARMED-WRITE.md`, `docs/H2H-house-grok.md`, `docs/H2H-house-grok.json`, `docs/H2H-house-grok.time`, `docs/POOL-research.md`, `docs/POOL-research-grok.md`, `docs/POOL-research-grok.json`, `docs/Q-CURSOR-VALUE-composer.md`, `docs/Q-CURSOR-VALUE-grok.md`, `docs/Q-CURSOR-VALUE-grok.json`, `docs/GROK-selfaudit.md`, `docs/GROK-selfaudit.json`, `docs/BASELINE-cursor-pro-20.md`, `docs/DISCORD-BRIEF.md`, `docs/AB-cursor-codex.md`, `docs/ab-review-task.md`, `docs/ask-grok-usage.md`, `docs/bakeoff-task.md`, `docs/headtohead-task.md`, `docs/pool-research-task.md`, `docs/q-cursor-value.md`, `docs/ticket-composer-001.md`, `docs/burn-1.md`, `docs/BURN-1.json`, `docs/sweep-gemini.md`, `docs/SWEEP-gemini.json`

EVIDENCE: One-run outputs. BENCH-LEDGER already holds the proven reserve facts. 25 sessions did not open these. They are the “still exist, still maintained, still rot” leftover of “lose no information.”

COST IF WRONG: A specific bakeoff paragraph is gone. Git history and BENCH-LEDGER remain. They would notice only if someone wanted the raw transcript of a single 2026-08-23 run.

---

DEFEND — what must NOT go, and why

- **`SPINE.md` PART I** (Ladder, Gate-0, Diagnose/Design fork, Reality Contract). First moves. Alive in spirit even when uncited. If these live only in a module, the orchestrator builds first and reads later.
- **`SPINE.md` PART III · THE TEN PRINCIPLES, especially 3, 6, 8, 10, and the invariant block in PART VIII.** Usage of the *heading* is 6. That is not grounds. Models follow “builder never reviews” / “gates pass, never it works” / “the boss merges” via THE COUNCIL, review-dispatch, and the copied invariant block without saying “THE TEN PRINCIPLES.” Deleting the numbered source of P3 is how the method dies.
- **`SPINE.md` PART IV · fleet test unique prongs** (Destined, Governed-where-it-RUNS, anti-laundering, declared-seat-lineage, continuity). The *name* is wallpaper. The content is the honest answer to today’s audit: vendor lanes are not this repo’s to close.
- **`SPINE.md` PART V mechanisms 5–6** (three lists + containment; untestability is never evidence). Never cited by heading. Unique. Cost of loss is confirmatory review — the scar in `SPINE-PROVENANCE.md`.
- **Doctrines 2, 3, 5 as named reflexes** (INSTRUMENT DON’T GUESS 16, SELF-VERIFY 18, RIGHT-SIZE 21). Alive. Doctrine 1’s **worktree isolation** sentence (lines 114–115) is unique; I am not voting the whole 5-gate pipeline away because of it.
- **THE COUNCIL (procedure + consent gate), THE METER LAW, THE TRANSPORT LAW, THE NOTATION, THE COUNCIL SEAT LAW clauses 1–6.** The usage table’s actually-invoked set. Recency inflates them; they are still the laws the shop argues with.
- **`SKILL.md` skeleton:** DEPENDS + load receipt, gold baton, seats table (lines 78–87), ON INVOCATION, byte-identical invariant block.
- **`mcp-seats/dispatch-guard.py` · `preflight`.** Honest accident-prevention for the Aug 21–22 empty-repo burn. Armcheck’s empty-repo canary can fail. Not a security boundary; a destination check.
- **`wmw_cursor_mcp.py` accident-prevention that already caught live bugs:** prompt spill (not argv), `_MODEL_RE` / UUID ids, credit/`UNKNOWN` fail-closed, YOLO allowlist, `_safe_cwd` (System32 / APPDATA), council lock, fail-closed on missing guard. Hygiene, not a fence — still worth keeping.
- **All three seat wrappers.** Near-identical JSON-RPC shells; vendor-specific guts (Grok deny list, agy flags, Cursor meters). Deleting a wrapper deletes a seat. Collapse would be a rewrite — out of scope.
- **`read-meters.py`, `bench-burn.py`, `calibrate-pool.py`.** Two burn tools are not duplicates: one reads a ledger, one sizes an unpublished pool, one reads vendor needles. METER LAW’s instruments.
- **`SPINE-WIRING.md`, `BENCH-LEDGER.md`, `VENDOR-CHECKLIST.md`, `SPINE-PROVENANCE.md`, `README.md`, `SETUP.md`, `docs/cursor-pool-classified.md`.** Not loaded on summon. Wiring, roster, “scripts cannot close cloud agents,” scars, human onboarding. Deleting these is how the next install re-derives gotchas.

---

THE ONE THING I would delete if I could only pick one

**`SPINE.md` PART VI plan-card posture playbooks (WAR CHEST / CRUISE / SHOESTRING / LIMP HOME and the ENTRY/MINIMAL/NONE essays).** Largest unused always-loaded block. The file it governs does not exist. It is the clearest proof of the owner’s diagnosis: law that sits in the trunk until models stop seeing any of it.

---

CONFIDENCE

**74.** Live-checked: no `PLAN-CARD.md`; `allowance.py` still cannot count calls; `dispatch-guard` yield was patched after reporting zero; wrapper now `import time`s and fails closed on a missing guard — today’s bugs were “fixed” by more code, which is the exhibit. Did not re-run the 25-session scan; trusted the table. Did not read every one-shot bakeoff to the last line. Wrapper coupling on `reserve` / `_allowance` is real: leftover calls fail loud, not silent.

⚫
